features: 7 weapons, each with its own projectile behaviour (the 14 pack variants were retired in 2.4.0)
25 total enemy types with late-run role diversity
5 biomes, one per boss cycle, each with its own floor, props, border, particles, light, hazard and enemy mix
55 run upgrades including 13 evolutions, no duplicates and rarer cards more often
18 persistent workshop modules
extended long-term milestones through wave 200 and high lifetime totals
dynamic wave director with 12+ encounter modes
procedural wave-specific obstacle additions with connectivity validation
dynamic vents, ice, acid pools, portals and supply caches; about five large hazards per wave
mode-specific enemy pool injections on later waves
biome-specific champion pools
high-wave scaling and boss progression retained
centralized v2.2 stat integration for new upgrades
additional weapon evolution synergies
new enemy behaviors for drone, driller, beacon and weaver
wave cache economy and persistent salvage interactions
Nova start-charge workshop progression
mobile pointer-id-aware synthetic-click suppression
viewport/orientation changes cancel active gameplay touch captures
resize/orientation follow-up timers are coalesced
bounded save parsing and snapshot sanitization retained
geometry-safe procedural spawn fallbacks retained
deterministic seeded wave and layout generation
runtime post-run diagnostics for arena, entities, input and errors
versioned game bundle and service-worker cache contract
orientation-any PWA manifest
browser-safe offline cache with mandatory core asset verification
expanded deterministic QA for weapons, enemies, waves, layouts and upgrades
25 enemy types with their own silhouettes, animation and death effects; a new player gunship
enemy and boss skins per biome
one boss per biome (5 bosses), Void Core and the Rift Core always last
one biome event per visit of a hazard biome: Meltdown, Whiteout, Spore Bloom, Rift Storm
signature enemies of a biome appear from its first wave
biome title card and boss intro card
Codex in Records: enemies, bosses and upgrades you have seen
updates apply on their own outside a run
5 biome music themes, each with a denser boss variant; own sounds for enemies, bosses, biome events and upgrade rarities
run history in Records
first-encounter enemy hints
live run monitor + post-run audit
tutorial and tips follow the input in use (keyboard/mouse or touch)
keyboard upgrade choice, settings from the pause menu, upgrade details in the pause build
optional run timer and FPS counter
changes: 3.0.0: traps — from wave 6 the arena fights back, with a skin per biome: floor strikes (Neon Yard electric plate, Ember Works piston crusher, Cryo Vault ice spikes, Toxin Marsh acid geyser, Void rift burst), sweeping beams from wave 9 (laser, flame jet, rift beam) and mines from wave 12 (mine, frost mine, spore pod, rift mine). Each warns first (ring, line, blinking light), hurts you and, as a share of their hull, enemies; chill, acid puddles and knock-back as side effects. None on boss waves. In Endless there are about half as many more, pauses and warnings are shorter, floor strikes hunt you from wave 40 and beams cross

3.0.0: Grenade gadget (key G, a GADGET button on touch screens): two charges, about 6 s to recharge one, thrown where you aim or at the densest group in sight, never into a wall; blast with knock-back and a slow; new cards Grenade Cells, Blast Core and Incendiary Mix (55 upgrades)

3.0.0: burst cap and a steeper Endless — from wave 40 an enemy can lose only a shrinking share of its hull within a quarter of a second (12% from about wave 148), however many shots, pierces, explosions and chain jumps land; Nova and bosses are exempt; regular enemies get +3% hull per wave beyond wave 30. A maxed Railgun used to wipe whole lines at wave 150. Damage numbers now show single attacks instead of running totals

3.0.0: new looks and sounds for it all — a model per trap skin, grenade with arc, landing marker and blast, a spark for resisted hits; 26 new sounds (grenade throw and blast, resisted hit, trap warnings, beams and strikes per skin, mine fuses)

2.9.1: no more stuck run when every upgrade is maxed — the wave end used to open an empty upgrade choice (reported at wave ~150) and the run could not go on; now the choice is skipped, the hull is repaired by 35% and a few shards are paid ("ALL UPGRADES MAXED" toast), and a saved run stuck on the empty choice resumes into the next wave

2.9.1: Ember Jet sounds like a flame — it fired 15 short noise bursts a second, which ticked and clicked; every shot now starts a soft, overlapping, sustained burst (low rumble, airy hiss, rare soft crackle), tested for steady loudness

2.9.1: fixes — long noise bursts (rocket, flame, event beds) are no longer cut off after about half a second; instanced arena props free their GPU buffers when the arena changes; a restored WebGL context is announced; the Weaver now announces its shot (lock-on sound and 0.45 s of aiming after the warp) and the Drone paths around obstacles instead of getting stuck on them

2.9.0: more detail in the arenas — every biome gets a detail layer (two draw calls per biome, placed from the arena seed): tall backdrop props outside the border (Neon Yard towers, containers and floodlights; Works smokestacks, furnaces and cranes; Vault ice spires and frozen wrecks; Toxin Marsh dead trees, giant mushrooms and bone piles; Void floating islands and crystal spires) and flat decals inside (chevrons, grates, soot and gears, frost patches, puddles and lily pads, rune circles), never on the start area

2.9.0: more detail on enemies and bosses — all 25 enemy types get a second pass (panels, vents, rivets, lamps, pupils, teeth, claws, tails, glow cores; 240-460 triangles each, same footprint and draw calls); Crucible and Frost Prism get the detail level of Warden, Queen and Core

2.9.0: sound — seven clearly different weapon shots (bright pew, fat shotgun, electric crackle, heavy rail with a metal tail, rising rocket whoosh, spinning-blade shing, pitchless flame roar), nine enemy death families, own shots for drones, turrets and bosses, a signature timbre and motif per boss (telegraphs, enrage, death), louder and denser event beds, a different pick sound per upgrade rarity, and a short music duck (at most 15% for 80 ms) on big hits; the music never pauses and notes survive a sound flood (tested)

2.8.1: fixes — upgrade cards stay visible with reduced motion; no crash when the Whiteout snow fades after going home; two tabs or windows no longer overwrite each other's save; Endless keeps the screen awake and its summary counts only the Endless part; Restart and Run Again keep the weapon and threat of the run; starting a new run over a stored one credits its shards; UI feedback toasts stay visible in the pause menu; dialogs take and return focus and Esc closes them from a text field; a held stick survives small viewport changes; a hanging network falls back to the cached page after 3 s; at most three save backups; formatCount shows millions

2.8.1: gameplay fixes — a resumed wave keeps its supply caches and bonus group; Endless bosses start from the wave-20 hull and keep growing; Resonance chains only by chance on non-Tesla weapons; elite splitters' mites are not elites; bosses' leftover adds and kills after death pay nothing; Rebound only bounces to enemies in sight; Echo volleys do not shift Overload and Overdrive; Rebound and Tungsten Core are not offered where they do nothing; Repair Beacon heals inside its ring only; Sentinel walks up when it has no line of sight; Weaver stops shooting a dead player; the Queen stops summoning in a crowded arena
2.8.1: sound — the music no longer stutters or drops out in heavy fights (shots and hits used to take its voices; it now has its own voice budget)
2.8.1: smaller — empty instance pools are not drawn, safe-area insets are cached

2.8.0: upgrade offers — fewer commons, more rare cards: the card weights are now 42/32/20/6 for common/rare/epic/legendary (were 60/28/10/2), and an offer is never made of commons only (its last card becomes a rare or better one)

2.8.0: five weak or overlapping upgrades are gone and their levels move to the one they resembled (old saves and pending offers are converted): Long Barrel → Targeting Chip (now also +8% range and +6% projectile speed), Tractor Field → Supply Loop (the workshop Magnet Coil keeps the pickup radius), Vector Capacitor → Servo Thrusters (now also -8% dash and Aegis cooldown per level), Glass Core → High-Yield Rounds, Momentum Core → Rapid Cycler; 52 upgrades

2.8.0: stronger commons and weak rares — High-Yield Rounds +18%, Reinforced Hull +25 HP, Targeting Chip, Cryo Rounds 25%, Shock Dash 60/90, Overload (every 5th shot, 45+15 per level, bigger burst), Acid Coating 22%, Apex Hunter +15%

2.8.0: smarter auto-aim — enemies behind a wall are not targeted any more (shots would only hit the wall; only the Lance slug, which flies through walls, may aim through them), close enemies come first (under 4 m strongly), rushers that explode, ram or jump at you (Bomber, Charger, Striker, Leaper, Sapper) are preferred a bit earlier, enemies that are immune right now (shield phase) only when nothing else is in reach, and the current target is kept while it is still a good one so the aim does not flicker; the manual aim assist skips enemies behind walls too

2.7.0: new look — the player drone is an arrow-shaped gunship (canopy, swept wings with glowing strips, twin thrusters whose flame follows speed, leans and banks); all 25 enemy types have new silhouettes with one memorable feature each (biological ones rounder and asymmetric, machines with panels, vents and lights); Warden, Hive Queen and Rift Core got more detail

2.7.0: enemies move with life — walk sway, hops, leaning into the movement direction, breathing or hovering at rest, hit squash, a spawn pop and a short shrink-and-spin death with a second debris burst (skipped on the battery preset); no extra geometry or draw calls
2.7.0: stronger biome skins — thicker lava veins with glow, frost rim and glints, more slime, violet void cracks; warning colours of attacks are unchanged

2.7.0: own sounds — six death sound families over the 25 enemies, telegraph sounds for charge, aim, fuse, mine and lob, one intro motif per boss plus telegraphs, enrage, phase and boss-down sounds, a boss variant of each biome's music (faster, extra voice), ambience and a cue for every biome event, a pick sound per upgrade rarity, reroll, card hover and wave-clear sounds, and a quiet engine hum; mixed through a limiter with a voice limit
2.6.0: touch sticks stay where the finger touched down: the centre no longer follows the finger when it is dragged far (move and aim)
2.6.0: the camera pan to a new boss lasts 3 s (was 1.5 s), the boss warning banner 3 s, the biome title card 3.5 s of its wave (was 1.6 s); input is never blocked by the cards

2.6.0: upgrades rebalanced after a bot benchmark (wave 14, all weapons): weaker — Resonance (+1 chain jump every 2nd level, +6% chain), Payload blast 30%+10%/level, Overcharge (Nova +30%), Chrono Dash 1.5 s, Overdrive Pulse (every 5th shot, double damage), Cluster Payload (2 bomblets, less damage); Split Chamber and Rebound are Epic now; stronger — Reactive Plating (30+20 damage, -4% fire rate), Targeting Chip (+10% crit and +0.06 crit multiplier), Rapid Cycler +15%, Servo Thrusters +10%, Long Barrel +25%, Cryo Rounds 20%, Vector Capacitor -10%, Last Stand -22%, Shock Dash 40/64, Overload, Combo Surge (60/90), Orbital Blades 18, Phantom Dash -50%, Dragon's Breath

2.6.0: Capacitor Bank is part of Overcharge (each kill adds 1% Nova charge per level) and Bounty Protocol part of Supply Loop (elite kills drop +1 shard per level); levels in old saves and pending offers move over; 57 upgrades
2.6.0: the workshop module Salvager is called Shard Refinery (the run upgrade keeps the name Salvager Core); Bloodrush cards show their cap

2.5.1: code refactor, no change to the game: the patches of the content packs and later fixes (methods wrapped from outside, up to eight times each) are folded into the classes and functions, so every method is in one place
2.5.1: about 3,600 minified local names (t, e, n …) are readable names; the minifier's syntax tricks (!0, comma chains, a && f() as a statement, var) are plain statements
2.5.1: the deep self-test has its own module (core/selftest.js); window.__riftTest uses the real names; Prettier formats the code and CI checks it
2.5.1: the save-sanitize health check expected the old High-Yield maximum 8 and reported FAIL since 2.5.0; it reads the maximum from the upgrade now

2.5.0: upgrades without duplicates — 19 weaker copies are folded into the upgrade they copied (e.g. Overbore Caliber and Kinetic Matrix into High-Yield Rounds, Afterburner and Cryo Coolant into Vector Capacitor, which now also shortens the Aegis cooldown); the kept upgrades have higher maximums, so a build reaches about the same totals. 59 upgrades, 13 evolutions unchanged

2.5.0: six new upgrades with their own mechanic — Cryo Skates (faster on ice and in Cryo Vault), Acid Coating (hits leave your own cyan acid, enemies in it take +25%), Heat Sink (fire-rate burst and Nova charge near lava or acid), Slipstream (+25% damage after a dash), Combo Surge (longer combos, a shockwave every 15 combo kills), Reactive Plating (a hit releases a repulse wave, -8% fire rate)

2.5.0: workshop — Rift Battery and Reactor Core are merged into Nova Cell (4 levels, at least 25% Nova per level at the start of each wave), Route Scanner into Field Supply (+1 cache and +50% cache shards per level); bought levels of the removed modules are refunded in full

2.5.0: three new workshop modules — Starter Kit (a random common upgrade per level at the start of a run), Hazard Attunement (+10% damage and +0.5 HP/s near a map hazard per level), Emergency Shield (once per wave below 30% hull: a short barrier and a repair)

2.5.0: stronger biomes — about five hazards per wave instead of three, about 25–30% larger (vents 1.7–2.2, ice 2.7–3.7, acid 2.2–3.0), kept clear of obstacles and further from the spawn; Void Core has two portal pairs in most waves

2.5.0: biome events, one per visit of a hazard biome (waves 2–4 of the visit, never a boss wave, +25% shards): Meltdown (Ember Works, extra vents that erupt together), Whiteout (Cryo Vault, snow storm with dense fog and more ice), Spore Bloom (Toxin Marsh, pools grow and new ones sprout), Rift Storm (Void Core, portals jump to new spots, shown 1.6 s ahead)
2.5.0: the signature enemies of a biome can appear from its first wave (at half weight until their normal unlock wave); Neon Yard is unchanged
2.5.0: biome title card on wave 1 and every biome change (name, hazard, boss) and a boss intro card during the camera pan to a new boss
